question: A red eight-sided (octagon) sign means:
choices: Slow down and go if clear
Yield only to traffic on the right
Stop only if other vehicles are present
explanation: An octagon is always a stop sign; a full stop is required.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A downward-pointing red-and-white triangle sign means:
choices: Yield the right-of-way, stopping if necessary
explanation: Yield signs require you to slow and give way to traffic on the through road.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A five-sided fluorescent yellow-green sign showing two children walking marks:
explanation: School zone signs are five-sided and fluorescent yellow-green.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond sign showing a deer means:
choices: A wildlife viewing area is ahead
Deer or other wildlife may cross the road ahead
Animals are not allowed on the road
explanation: It warns of wildlife crossings; slow down and scan the roadside.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A diamond sign showing a child running with a ball warns of:
choices: A crosswalk with a crossing guard
explanation: The playground sign warns that children may be nearby.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A white X-shaped sign (crossbuck) at the side of the road marks:
explanation: The crossbuck is posted at railway crossings; trains have the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A railway crossbuck with a small sign below it reading "2" means:
choices: There are two sets of tracks to cross
explanation: The number shows how many tracks; another train may be coming on the other track.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a crossbuck (X) symbol means:
explanation: This advance warning sign tells you to prepare for a railway crossing.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A sign with a red circle and slash over a left-pointing turn arrow means:
explanation: A red circle with a slash prohibits the action shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A sign with a red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow means:
explanation: The slash prohibits the U-turn shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: On a regulatory sign, a green circle around a symbol means:
choices: A warning of a hazard ahead
explanation: Green circles show permitted actions; red circles with slashes show prohibited ones.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A rectangular white sign with black letters or symbols usually:
choices: States a rule you must obey
explanation: White rectangular signs are regulatory signs.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond sign showing a curved arrow means:
explanation: Curve warning signs tell you to slow before the bend.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A curve warning sign with a "40 km/h" tab below it means:
choices: 40 km/h is the advised safe speed for the curve
The speed limit everywhere is now 40 km/h
explanation: Yellow speed tabs give the recommended maximum for good conditions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing two lanes joining into one means:
choices: Lanes merge ahead; adjust speed and space to merge
explanation: Merge signs warn that traffic will need to share one lane.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond with one arrow pointing up and one pointing down means:
explanation: Expect oncoming traffic, often where a divided road ends.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a truck on a downward slope means:
explanation: Slow down and use a lower gear on a steep downgrade.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a car with wavy skid marks means:
choices: The road is slippery when wet
explanation: Reduce speed on wet pavement where this sign is posted.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a person walking means:
explanation: This warning sign tells you to expect pedestrians.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a bicycle means:
explanation: Share the road and give cyclists safe passing room.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a traffic light symbol means:
choices: The signals ahead are not working
explanation: Be ready to stop at the upcoming signal.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a stop sign symbol means:
explanation: Prepare to stop at the sign ahead.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a T shape means:
choices: The road ends ahead; you must turn left or right
A side road joins from the right
explanation: This T-intersection sign warns that the road does not continue straight.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a plus (+) symbol means:
choices: A first aid station is ahead
explanation: Watch for vehicles entering from the crossroad.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: An orange diamond sign showing a worker with a shovel means:
choices: Road work ahead; slow down and watch for workers
explanation: Orange signs warn of construction and maintenance zones.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A traffic control person holds up a sign reading "STOP". You must:
choices: Stop and wait until they signal you to go
Stop only if workers are on the road
explanation: Traffic control persons' directions must be obeyed.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: An orange triangle with a red border on the back of a vehicle means:
explanation: Slow-moving vehicle signs warn you to slow and pass only when safe.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A white diamond symbol on a sign over a lane or painted in it marks:
choices: A reserved lane for certain vehicles
explanation: White diamonds mark lanes reserved for buses, HOVs or others shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A reserved-lane sign shows a white diamond and "2+". This lane is for:
choices: Vehicles with at least two people in them
explanation: HOV lanes are for vehicles carrying the number of people shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Green rectangular signs with white lettering usually give:
explanation: Green guide signs provide route and destination information.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Brown signs along a highway usually point to:
explanation: Brown signs mark parks, campgrounds and attractions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Blue signs along a highway usually tell you about:
choices: Services such as gas, food or lodging
explanation: Blue signs show nearby services.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A red circle with a slash over a walking person means:
explanation: Pedestrians may not use that road or area.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A red circle with a slash over a bicycle means:
explanation: The slash prohibits bicycles on that road.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A red circle with a white horizontal bar means:
explanation: Do not enter signs stop you from going the wrong way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A black-and-white sign with an arrow and "ONE WAY" means:
choices: Turn only in the arrow's direction
Traffic moves only in the arrow's direction
explanation: On a one-way street, all traffic travels in the direction shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A sign showing an arrow curving to the right of a median island means:
choices: Keep to the right of the island
explanation: Keep-right signs direct traffic past a median or obstacle.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A sign showing curved arrows turning left from both directions into a centre lane marks:
choices: A passing lane for both directions
explanation: Drivers from both directions use the centre lane only to turn left.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing two lines angling in toward each other means:
explanation: Narrowing-road signs warn that there is less space ahead.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A sign at a crossing showing a person walking on a striped crosswalk marks:
choices: A pedestrian crosswalk; yield to pedestrians
explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A fluorescent yellow-green sign showing children on a crosswalk marks:
explanation: School crosswalk warnings use fluorescent yellow-green.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A school zone sign shows a "30 km/h" tab with no times. The limit applies:
choices: From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days
From dawn to dusk every day
Only when a crossing guard is present
explanation: Unposted school zone limits apply 8 a.m.–5 p.m. on school days.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A playground zone sign has a "30 km/h" tab. The limit applies:
choices: 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days
Every day from dawn to dusk
explanation: Playground zone limits apply dawn to dusk, every day.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A white sign reading "KEEP RIGHT EXCEPT TO PASS" means:
choices: Use the right lane unless you are passing
Only trucks may use the left lane
Stay right of the centre median
explanation: Slower traffic keeps right and uses the left lane to pass.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A white sign with a red circle and slash over a letter "P" means:
choices: No parking in the area shown
explanation: This regulatory sign prohibits parking in the area or times shown.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: An overhead lane sign shows an arrow pointing straight and one curving right. That lane may be used to:
explanation: Lane-use signs show the movements allowed from that lane.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing a snake-like arrow means:
explanation: Expect a series of curves; slow down.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A yellow diamond showing rocks falling from a slope means:
choices: Do not stop on the shoulder ever
Watch for falling rock on the road
explanation: Rock fall signs warn of debris that may be on the road.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A row of yellow signs with black arrowheads (chevrons) on a curve means:
choices: A sharp curve; follow the direction of the arrows
explanation: Chevrons outline sharp curves and show their direction.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Most warning signs are:
explanation: Yellow diamonds warn of hazards or changes ahead.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who goes first?
explanation: At the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
choices: The first vehicle to come to a complete stop
The vehicle on the wider road
explanation: First to stop is first to go.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: At a four-way stop, two vehicles stop at the same time. Who goes first?
explanation: When tied, the vehicle on the right goes first.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: You are turning left on a green light (no arrow). You must yield to:
choices: Oncoming traffic going straight and pedestrians
explanation: Left-turning drivers yield to oncoming through traffic and pedestrians.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: At a yield sign with traffic on the through road, you should:
choices: Always come to a full stop
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Slow down, stop if needed, and wait for a safe gap
explanation: You may enter without stopping only if the way is clear.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: When entering a traffic circle or roundabout, you must:
choices: Enter first if you are on the right
Stop and wait for a signal
Yield to traffic already in the circle
explanation: Traffic in the circle has the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: In a BC traffic circle, you travel:
explanation: Go around to the right, counterclockwise.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A traffic circle has no signs. You should treat it like:
explanation: Without a sign, uncontrolled-intersection rules apply.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Leaving a driveway or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must:
choices: Stop before the sidewalk and yield to pedestrians and traffic
explanation: Drivers entering a road from a lane or driveway yield to everyone.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A pedestrian is in an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. You must:
choices: Proceed; unmarked crosswalks have no rules
Yield only if there is a sign
explanation: Unmarked crosswalks exist at intersections; pedestrians in them have the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A vehicle ahead in the next lane is stopped at a crosswalk. You should:
choices: Pass carefully on the other side
explanation: It may be stopped for a pedestrian you cannot see.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Your light is green but traffic is backed up into the intersection. You should:
choices: Enter and stop in the middle
Go, since you have a green
Wait until there is room to clear the intersection
explanation: Never block an intersection.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Turning right on a green light, you must yield to:
choices: Pedestrians crossing the road you are turning onto
explanation: Watch for and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is crossing. You must:
choices: Honk so they know you are there
Always yield and give them plenty of room
explanation: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired must always be given the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: Merging onto a highway from an acceleration lane, you should:
choices: Stop at the end of the ramp
Match highway speed and yield to traffic already on it
Expect highway traffic to let you in
explanation: Merging traffic adjusts speed to fit into a safe gap.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Traffic lights at an intersection are not working. You should:
choices: Go through if no one is close
Follow the car ahead without stopping
Treat it as a four-way stop
explanation: Dark signals mean everyone stops and takes turns.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: If you are unsure who has the right-of-way, you should:
choices: Yield to the other road user
Take it, so you don't confuse others
Speed up to clear the intersection
explanation: It's always better to yield when in doubt.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: The right-of-way is best described as something that is:
choices: Always held by the driver on the left
explanation: Rules say who should yield; no one is entitled to force it.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: When changing lanes, who must yield?
choices: Vehicles in the other lane, once you signal
You, to vehicles already in the lane you are entering
explanation: A signal does not give you the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you are turning left and an oncoming car is going straight. Who goes first?
explanation: Left-turning vehicles yield to oncoming through traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A bus at a stop flashes a "yield" sign on its back while signalling to pull out. You should:
choices: Stop only if there are passengers
explanation: BC drivers must yield to buses re-entering traffic in lower-speed areas.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: You are turning right across a bike lane. You must:
choices: Turn from the lane to the left of the bike lane without checking
Shoulder check and yield to cyclists in the lane
explanation: Cyclists going straight have the right-of-way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: You hear a siren and see flashing lights behind you. You must:
choices: Speed up to get out of the way
Stop where you are, even in an intersection
Keep going at the same speed
Pull to the right edge, stop, and wait until it passes
explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles by moving right and stopping, not in an intersection.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.177

question: Two vehicles meet at a four-way stop: you are going straight and the vehicle opposite is turning left. You both stopped together. Who goes first?
explanation: Left turns yield to oncoming through traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A pedestrian starts crossing on a "Don't Walk" signal as your light turns green. You should:
choices: Go, since you have a green
Wait for them to finish crossing
explanation: Always yield to pedestrians on the roadway to avoid a collision.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit in a BC city or town is:
explanation: The default municipal limit is 50 km/h.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit on a BC highway outside cities is:
explanation: The default limit outside municipalities is 80 km/h.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: The speed limit in a BC school zone during its hours is:
explanation: School zones are 30 km/h during the posted or default hours.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: The speed limit in a BC playground zone is:
explanation: Playground zones are 30 km/h from dawn to dusk.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: It's 7 p.m. on a sunny July Saturday and you pass a 30 km/h playground zone. You must drive:
choices: The normal limit, since it's the weekend
The normal limit, since it's after 5 p.m.
explanation: Playground zones apply every day until dusk.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: It's 4 p.m. on a school day and you approach a school zone with no times posted. You must drive:
choices: The normal limit if no children are visible
explanation: Unposted school zones apply 8 a.m.–5 p.m. on school days.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A posted speed limit is the:
choices: Maximum speed allowed in ideal conditions
explanation: Slow below the limit when conditions are poor.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: In BC, "excessive speeding" means driving:
choices: More than 10 km/h over the limit
More than 20 km/h over the limit
More than 40 km/h over the limit
More than 60 km/h over the limit
explanation: Over 40 km/h above the limit is excessive speeding.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: excessive speed and careless driving

question: For a first excessive speeding offence, police can impound the vehicle for:
explanation: First offence impoundment is 7 days.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: excessive speed and careless driving

question: Passing a stopped vehicle with flashing lights where the limit is 80 km/h or more, you must slow to no more than:
explanation: Slow Down, Move Over: 70 km/h on roads posted 80+.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: Passing a stopped vehicle with flashing lights where the limit is under 80 km/h, you must slow to no more than:
explanation: Slow Down, Move Over: 40 km/h on roads posted under 80.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: It's raining heavily on a highway posted at 100 km/h. You should:
choices: Drive at 100 km/h to keep up
Drive slower than the limit to suit conditions
Drive at 100 km/h with hazard lights on
Drive faster to get out of the rain
explanation: Limits are for ideal conditions; adjust to weather.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: If you double your speed, your braking distance becomes about:
explanation: Braking distance grows with the square of speed.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic on a highway can:
choices: Earn you a lower insurance rate
Create a hazard by causing others to pass
explanation: Large speed differences increase passing and conflicts.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: A yellow speed tab under a warning sign is:
choices: An advised safe speed for that hazard
explanation: Advisory speeds suggest the safe speed in good conditions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: At night on an unlit road, you should drive at a speed that lets you:
choices: Keep up with the posted limit
Stop within the distance your headlights light up
explanation: Don't overdrive your headlights.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Speed limit signs in a construction zone must be:
choices: Followed only when workers are visible
Obeyed like any other speed limit
explanation: Construction signs carry instructions you must obey.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A second excessive speeding offence within two years can mean an impoundment of:
explanation: Repeat offences bring longer impoundments.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: excessive speed and careless driving

question: The legal blood alcohol limit for a BC L or N driver is:
explanation: GLP drivers must have no alcohol in their blood.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: A new (L or N) driver found with any alcohol in their system faces:
explanation: Any alcohol means a 12-hour roadside suspension for GLP drivers.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: driving while affected by drugs or alcohol

question: The zero-tolerance rule for L and N drivers also covers:
explanation: GLP drivers must have zero alcohol and zero drugs in their blood.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: For a fully licensed driver, the BC "warn" range for blood alcohol is:
explanation: A warn reading is 0.05 to below 0.08.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: A fully licensed driver's first warn reading in five years brings a driving prohibition of:
explanation: First warn: 3 days.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: A second warn reading within five years brings a prohibition of:
explanation: Second warn: 7 days.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: A third warn reading within five years brings a prohibition of:
explanation: Third warn: 30 days.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: A fully licensed driver who blows a "fail" (0.08 or more) gets a prohibition of:
explanation: A fail reading brings a 90-day IRP.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: Refusing to give a breath sample at the roadside is treated like:
choices: No offence if you are sober
explanation: Refusal carries the same penalty as a fail.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: With a fail or refusal, the vehicle is usually impounded for:
explanation: Fail and refusal IRPs come with a 30-day impoundment.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: After drinking, the only thing that lowers your blood alcohol is:
explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: Which ability does alcohol usually affect first?
explanation: Alcohol impairs judgment early, so drinkers often think they're fine.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: Cannabis can affect driving by:
choices: Making you more alert at night
Slowing reaction time and impairing judgment
Having no effect after one hour
explanation: Driving while affected by cannabis is dangerous and illegal.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: Before driving after taking a prescription or cold medicine, you should:
choices: Assume it is safe because it is legal
Check the label or ask a pharmacist about effects on driving
explanation: Many legal medications cause drowsiness or impairment.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: Combining alcohol with cannabis or other drugs usually:
explanation: Mixing substances multiplies their effects.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: A fully licensed driver gets a warn reading. Besides the prohibition, police may also:
explanation: Warn IRPs can include a vehicle impoundment.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: alcohol and drug related prohibitions

question: A novice (N) driver's licence is suspended for alcohol. What happens to their novice stage?
choices: They go straight to a full licence
explanation: A suspension resets the novice period.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: driving while affected by drugs or alcohol

question: Which of these affects how quickly your blood alcohol rises?
choices: Your body weight and whether you have eaten
Whether you drink from a glass or can
explanation: Body size, food and amount consumed all affect BAC.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: As of October 19, 2026, an L driver's supervisor must be at least:
explanation: The minimum supervisor age dropped from 25 to 22.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: An L driver's supervisor must hold:
choices: A full Class 5 (or higher) licence without a zero-alcohol restriction
Any valid licence, including an N
explanation: The supervisor needs a full licence of their own.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/graduated-licensing-program-changes

question: Where must an L driver's supervisor sit?
choices: In the front passenger seat beside the learner
explanation: The supervisor sits beside the learner.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: Besides the supervisor, an L driver may carry:
choices: One passenger, or more if they are immediate family
explanation: Extra passengers are limited to one unless they are immediate family.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: An L driver may NOT drive between:
explanation: Learners are restricted from midnight to 5 a.m.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: An L driver must display:
choices: An L sign only at night
A red L sign on the back of the vehicle
explanation: The L sign must be shown while driving.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: Can an L driver use a hands-free phone while driving?
choices: No, no electronic devices are allowed, even hands-free
explanation: L drivers may not use any electronic device while driving.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: The minimum age to get a Class 7L licence in BC is:
explanation: You can get your L on or after your 16th birthday.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/Get-your-L

question: A driver under 25 must hold an L for at least how long before the Class 7 road test?
explanation: Under-25 learners keep the 12-month learner stage.
source: news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2026PSSG0061-000847

question: Under the October 2026 changes, a learner aged 25 or older must hold an L for at least:
explanation: The learner stage for 25+ drops from 12 to 9 months.
source: news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2026PSSG0061-000847

question: A novice driver under 25 must display:
explanation: Under-25 Class 7 drivers display the N sign.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7-licence-and-youre-under-25

question: A novice driver under 25 may carry how many passengers without a supervisor?
choices: One, unless the others are immediate family
explanation: N drivers under 25 are limited to one passenger unless all extras are immediate family.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7-licence-and-youre-under-25

question: Can a novice (N) driver use a hands-free phone while driving?
choices: No, no electronic devices, even hands-free
explanation: N drivers may not use electronic devices while driving.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7-licence-and-youre-under-25

question: For a driver under 25, the novice stage normally lasts:
explanation: Under 25: 24 months of safe driving.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/graduated-licensing-program-changes

question: A driver under 25 who completes an ICBC-approved GLP course can shorten the novice stage to:
explanation: The approved course cuts the N stage by 6 months.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/graduated-licensing-program-changes

question: Under the October 2026 changes, a novice driver aged 25 or older needs how much safe driving before assessment?
explanation: Drivers 25+ need 12 months.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/graduated-licensing-program-changes

question: Since October 19, 2026, what replaces the second road test for moving from Class 7 to Class 5?
explanation: A clean record now earns the move through a Driving Record Assessment.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/graduated-licensing-program-changes

question: After passing the Driving Record Assessment, a driver gets a Class 5 licence with:
choices: A 12-month zero alcohol and drug restriction
explanation: A 12-month restricted period follows, with zero BAC and zero drugs.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7-licence-and-youre-under-25

question: During the novice stage, which conviction restarts the novice period?
choices: A seatbelt warning given to a passenger
Using an electronic device while driving
explanation: Excessive speed or device convictions restart the novice period.
source: news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2026PSSG0061-000847

question: For GLP passenger rules, which passenger counts as immediate family?
explanation: Immediate family includes parents, children, spouse, siblings and grandparents.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.9 (your licence)

question: Once a novice driver turns 25, which restriction no longer applies?
explanation: Alcohol and device rules still apply after 25.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.9 (your licence)

question: An L driver under 25 is driving with a qualified supervisor, a younger brother and a sister. This is:
choices: Not allowed; only one passenger is allowed
Allowed, because the extra passengers are immediate family
explanation: The passenger limit does not apply to immediate family.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: A novice driver under 25 can carry several friends if:
choices: A qualified supervisor (22+) is also in the vehicle
explanation: A qualified supervisor lifts the one-passenger limit.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7-licence-and-youre-under-25

question: What does the zero blood alcohol rule allow an L or N driver to drink before driving?
explanation: Zero means zero.
source: icbc.com/driver-licensing/new-drivers/you-have-a-class-7l-licence

question: The main purpose of BC's Graduated Licensing Program is to:
choices: Let new drivers gain experience under lower-risk conditions
Let teens skip the road test
explanation: Restrictions reduce risk while skills develop.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.9 (your licence)

question: You must not park within how many metres of a fire hydrant?
explanation: No parking within 5 m of a hydrant.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road) / Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.189

question: You must not park within how many metres of the approach side of a crosswalk?
explanation: No parking within 6 m before a crosswalk.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.189

question: You must not park within how many metres of a stop sign or traffic light?
explanation: No parking within 6 m of a stop sign or signal.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: You must not park within how many metres of the nearest rail of a railway crossing?
explanation: No parking within 15 m of the nearest rail.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: When parallel parking at a curb, your wheels must be within:
explanation: Park parallel and within 30 cm of the curb.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Parking downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
explanation: The curb stops the car from rolling into traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
explanation: If it rolls back, the tire catches the curb.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Parking uphill on a road with no curb, turn your front wheels:
choices: To the right, toward the road's edge
explanation: The car would roll away from traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: In a manual transmission car parked facing downhill, leave it in:
explanation: Reverse downhill; first gear uphill or on level ground.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Which is NOT a legal place to park?
choices: At a curb 10 m from a hydrant
At a curb 20 m from a crosswalk
Across the entrance to a driveway
explanation: Never block a driveway, lane or intersection.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: When you park on the street, your vehicle should face:
choices: The same direction as traffic in that lane
explanation: Your right-side wheels must be next to the curb.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.190

question: Before pulling out from a parallel parking spot, you should:
choices: Signal, shoulder check and wait for a safe gap
Pull out quickly before traffic arrives
explanation: Check your blind spot and yield to traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Before opening your door after parking on a street, you should:
choices: Open it quickly to get out of the way
Check for cyclists and traffic behind you
explanation: Opening a door into a cyclist's path can cause a serious crash.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A fire truck has stopped to answer an alarm. You must not park within:
choices: 150 m of it on the same road
explanation: Keep 150 m away from stopped fire apparatus.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.198

question: Which of these is a legal place to park?
choices: At a curb 7 m from a crosswalk
explanation: Beyond 6 m from a crosswalk is allowed if no signs prohibit it.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: If you must stop on a highway outside a city, you should:
choices: Stop in the right lane with hazards on
Stop on a curve where it's flat
Pull completely off the travelled lanes if possible
explanation: Keep the road clear and your vehicle visible.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A steady yellow traffic light means:
choices: Speed up to beat the red
Stop if you can do so safely; otherwise go through carefully
Proceed; the light is about to turn green
explanation: Yellow warns the light is about to turn red.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution
The light is broken; treat it as green
explanation: Flashing yellow is a caution signal.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A flashing red traffic light means:
choices: Stop, then go only when it is safe
The light is about to turn green
explanation: Flashing red works like a stop sign.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: In BC, a flashing green light usually means:
choices: Speed up; it will turn red
A pedestrian-controlled light; go with caution
explanation: Pedestrians can change it to yellow then red.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: At a red light, you may turn right:
choices: After a full stop, yielding to all, unless a sign forbids it
explanation: Right on red is allowed after stopping and yielding.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A left turn on a red light is allowed only:
choices: From a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping
explanation: Only one-way to one-way, after a full stop and yielding.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A green left-turn arrow with a green light means:
choices: You must yield to oncoming traffic
You may turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
explanation: The arrow gives a protected left turn.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: To signal a left turn by hand, you:
choices: Extend your left arm straight out
explanation: Arm straight out means left.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: To signal a right turn by hand, you:
choices: Extend your left arm straight out
Point right with your right hand
Bend your left arm upward at the elbow
explanation: Arm bent up means right.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: To signal that you are slowing or stopping by hand, you:
choices: Extend your left arm straight out
explanation: Arm bent down means slowing or stopping.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Yellow lines on the road separate:
explanation: Yellow divides opposing traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: White lines between lanes separate:
choices: Traffic moving in the same direction
explanation: White lines divide lanes going the same way.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: On a two-lane road, a solid yellow line is on your side with a broken line beside it. You:
explanation: A solid line on your side means no passing.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A double solid yellow centre line means:
choices: Passing allowed only on the right
explanation: Neither side may cross to pass.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A broken white line between lanes means:
choices: The lane is about to end
You may change lanes when it is safe
The lane is for buses only
explanation: Broken lines permit crossing when safe.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: A solid white line between lanes going the same direction means:
choices: You should stay in your lane
The lane is for turning only
explanation: Solid white lines discourage lane changes.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: At a stop sign with a painted stop line, you must stop:
choices: With your front wheels on the line
At the edge of the cross street
explanation: Stop at the line, then before the crosswalk or intersection if none.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.186

question: On a multi-lane highway you should usually:
choices: Drive on the shoulder when slow
explanation: The left lane is for passing.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Before changing lanes you should:
choices: Check mirrors, signal, and shoulder check your blind spot
explanation: Mirrors don't show blind spots; shoulder check.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Passing on the right is:
choices: Allowed only when safe, never by driving on the shoulder
explanation: You may pass on the right on multi-lane roads or a vehicle turning left, without using the shoulder.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: You should use your turn signal:
choices: Only when other cars are nearby
Before turning, changing lanes or pulling away from a curb
explanation: Signal early so others know your intentions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: After completing a turn, your signal does not shut off. You should:
explanation: A forgotten signal misleads other drivers.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A lane marked with white diamonds may be used:
choices: Only by the vehicles and at the times the signs allow
explanation: Reserved lanes are for buses, HOVs or others shown on signs.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: Railway crossing lights are flashing. You must stop:
choices: No closer than 5 m and no farther than 15 m from the nearest rail
Right on the tracks if clear
explanation: Stop 5–15 m from the nearest rail until it's safe.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) / Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: A yellow arrow follows a green left-turn arrow. This means:
choices: Oncoming traffic now has a red
explanation: Be prepared to stop; the protected phase is ending.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.3 (signs, signals, road markings)

question: In good conditions, keep a following distance of at least:
explanation: Two seconds is the minimum in good conditions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: On high-speed roads, increase your following distance to at least:
explanation: Use three seconds at highway speeds.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: In bad weather or on slippery roads, increase your following distance to at least:
explanation: Four seconds in poor conditions.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Behind a large truck or a motorcycle, keep at least:
explanation: Trucks block your view and motorcycles can stop quickly.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: You must use your headlights from:
choices: 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
One hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
Only when it is fully dark
explanation: BC requires headlights half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: You must also turn on your headlights when you cannot see clearly for:
explanation: Use lights when visibility drops below 150 m.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: You must dim your high beams when within how far of another vehicle (meeting or following)?
explanation: Switch to low beams within 150 m.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Low beam headlights light up the road about how far ahead?
explanation: Low beams reach about 30 m; high beams about 100 m.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Hydroplaning happens when:
choices: Snow builds up under the vehicle
Tires ride on a film of water and lose contact with the road
explanation: You lose steering and braking control.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to:
choices: Slow down in heavy rain and keep tires in good condition
explanation: Lower speed keeps tires in contact with the road.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
choices: Low beam headlights and reduce speed
Hazard lights while moving at full speed
explanation: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Ice often forms first on:
explanation: Bridges cool faster than other road surfaces.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Roads are often most slippery:
choices: Just after it starts to rain
Right after a street sweeper passes
explanation: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road surface.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: If you start to lose traction in a curve, you should:
choices: Ease off the accelerator and avoid braking
explanation: Reapply gas gently once traction returns.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: With anti-lock brakes (ABS) in an emergency stop, you should:
choices: Press firmly and keep steady pressure; don't pump
explanation: ABS lets you brake hard and still steer.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: On gravel, compared with ordinary brakes, ABS braking distance may be:
explanation: ABS doesn't always shorten stopping distance.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, the safest thing to do is:
choices: Pull over somewhere safe and rest
Open the window and keep going
Drive faster to get home sooner
explanation: Only rest cures fatigue.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: An oncoming driver's high beams are blinding you. You should:
choices: Turn on your high beams too
Look toward the right edge of your lane
explanation: Glancing right keeps you on course without the glare.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: You see one deer cross the road ahead. You should:
choices: Slow down and watch for more animals
explanation: Animals often travel in groups.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Before driving on a snowy morning, you must:
choices: Clear snow and ice from all windows and lights
Clear only a small hole in the windshield
explanation: You need full visibility to drive safely.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Passing is most dangerous:
choices: On a road with broken lines
Near the top of a hill or on a curve
explanation: You can't see oncoming traffic there.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.4 (rules of the road)

question: Why must you shoulder check before changing lanes?
choices: It is only required on road tests
Mirrors don't show your blind spots
explanation: A quick look over your shoulder covers the blind spot.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Using a hands-free phone while driving (for a full-licence driver) is:
choices: Safer than talking to a passenger in every case
Still a distraction that can slow your reactions
explanation: Conversation draws attention away from driving.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: On a long trip, a good way to fight fatigue is to:
choices: Take a break about every two hours
explanation: Regular breaks help you stay alert.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.7 (personal strategies)

question: When driving at night, you should:
choices: Drive at the speed limit with high beams always on
Follow closely to use the car ahead's lights
Increase following distance and slow down
explanation: Visibility is reduced at night.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: On a road with a limit of 50 km/h or less, you must pass a cyclist with at least:
explanation: BC's minimum passing distance is 1 m at 50 km/h or less.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: On a road with a limit over 50 km/h, you must pass a cyclist with at least:
explanation: Over 50 km/h, the minimum is 1.5 m.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: Passing a cyclist who is in a protected bike lane, you must leave at least:
explanation: A 0.5 m minimum applies to sidewalks and protected lanes.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: BC's safe passing distance rules protect which road users?
choices: Pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and scooter riders
explanation: All vulnerable road users are covered.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: A school bus ahead has flashing red lights. You must:
choices: Stop, whether you are behind it or meeting it
explanation: Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: After stopping for a school bus, you may go when:
choices: The children are on the sidewalk
The lights stop flashing and the stop sign is pulled in, or the bus moves
explanation: Wait until the bus signals it's safe.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: If you can't see a large truck's mirrors, then:
choices: You are at a safe distance
The truck is about to stop
The truck driver can't see you
You should pass on the right
explanation: Stay out of a truck's blind spots.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A large truck ahead swings left before turning right. You should:
choices: Stay back and not pass on its right
explanation: Trucks need extra room to make right turns.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A motorcycle is in your lane ahead. You should:
choices: Pass it within the same lane
Give it the full lane; never share the lane
explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A train is approaching a crossing. You should remember that:
choices: You can safely beat the train
explanation: Never try to race a train.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: After a train passes a multi-track crossing, you should:
choices: Check for a second train before crossing
explanation: Another train may be coming on another track.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: You are approaching a person riding a horse. You should:
choices: Honk so they know you're there
Slow down, pass wide and avoid honking
explanation: Sudden noise can startle the animal.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: A ball rolls onto the road from between parked cars. You should:
choices: Slow down and expect a child to follow
explanation: Children may run out after it.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: "Slow down, move over" applies to stopped vehicles with flashing lights that are:
choices: Red, blue, yellow or white, including tow trucks
explanation: It covers all vehicles authorized to show flashing lights.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: On a multi-lane road, when passing a stopped vehicle with flashing lights, you should also:
choices: Move into another lane if it's safe
Stay in the lane closest to it
explanation: Give roadside workers room.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: On a divided highway, the slow down, move over rule does not apply when the stopped vehicle is:
choices: On the other side, facing opposing traffic
explanation: The exception covers vehicles approached from the opposite direction.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: Unless you are driving an emergency vehicle, you must not follow a fire truck answering an alarm within:
explanation: Stay 150 m back from fire apparatus.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.198

question: A cyclist ahead holds their right arm straight out. They are signalling:
explanation: BC lets cyclists signal right turns with the right arm.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.171

question: Pedestrians are most at risk:
choices: At night and when wearing dark clothing
explanation: They are hard to see in low light.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: When passing a cyclist, the safe distance is measured:
choices: From your tire to their tire
From your mirror to the cyclist's handlebar
explanation: Measure from the outermost parts of each.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: When following a motorcycle, you should allow extra distance because:
explanation: Leave at least three seconds behind a motorcycle.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.5 (see-think-do)

question: Before turning right, you should check for:
choices: Nothing if your signal is on
Cyclists and pedestrians on your right
explanation: Shoulder check for cyclists coming up on your right.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.6 (sharing the road)

question: The ICBC Class 7 knowledge test has how many questions?
explanation: The car knowledge test has 50 multiple-choice questions.
source: ICBC 'Before you take your knowledge test' tip sheet

question: To pass the knowledge test, you need at least:
explanation: The pass mark is 80%.
source: ICBC 'Before you take your knowledge test' tip sheet

question: A ticket for using an electronic device while driving carries a fine and:
explanation: Distracted driving tickets add 4 points.
source: icbc.com/road-safety/crashes-happen/distracted-driving

question: The fine on a BC distracted driving ticket is:
explanation: Each ticket carries a $368 fine.
source: icbc.com/road-safety/crashes-happen/distracted-driving

question: Two distracted driving offences in one year trigger:
choices: An automatic driving record review that may lead to a prohibition
explanation: Repeat offenders may be prohibited from 3 to 12 months.
source: icbc.com/road-safety/crashes-happen/distracted-driving

question: If you have 4 or more penalty points at the end of a 12-month period, you:
choices: Pay a Driver Penalty Point premium
explanation: Penalty points cost money through ICBC premiums.
source: icbc.com/road-safety/crashes-happen/distracted-driving

question: A ticket for driving more than 40 km/h over the limit carries:
explanation: Excessive speed is costly.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: excessive speed and careless driving

question: Not slowing down and moving over for a stopped vehicle with flashing lights can bring:
explanation: It is a ticketable offence.
source: gov.bc.ca: Slow down, move over

question: Failing to give a vulnerable road user the minimum passing distance can bring:
explanation: Unsafe passing is penalized.
source: gov.bc.ca: Sharing the road safely (vulnerable road users)

question: You successfully dispute an excessive speeding ticket. The vehicle impoundment:
choices: Is cancelled and the costs refunded
Still stands, and the owner pays the costs
explanation: The owner still pays towing and storage.
source: gov.bc.ca RoadSafetyBC: excessive speed and careless driving

question: In BC, a child must use a booster seat until they are:
choices: 9 years old or 145 cm tall, whichever comes first
explanation: Boosters are required until age 9 or 145 cm.
source: ICBC child car seats guidance

question: Who is responsible for making sure passengers under 16 wear seatbelts?
explanation: Drivers must ensure young passengers are buckled up.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.220

question: An emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches while you're in an intersection. You should:
choices: Clear the intersection, then pull right and stop
Stop in the middle of the intersection
Speed up and stay ahead of it
explanation: Never stop inside an intersection for an emergency vehicle.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.177

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
choices: Look at what you are trying to avoid
Look and steer where you want to go
Turn the wheel the opposite way you want to go
explanation: Your hands follow your eyes.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: If a front tire blows out, you should:
choices: Grip the wheel firmly and ease off the gas
explanation: Keep control and slow gradually.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: If your brakes fail, you should first:
explanation: Pumping may restore pressure; then downshift and use the parking brake gently.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: If your accelerator sticks, you should:
choices: Turn off the ignition and remove the key
explanation: Neutral disconnects the engine power from the wheels.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: Your vehicle stalls on railway tracks and a train is coming. You should:
choices: Get everyone out and move well away from the tracks
Push the car off the tracks
explanation: Get out immediately; vehicles can't win against trains.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: You arrive first at a crash where someone is hurt. You should:
choices: Move the injured person right away
Park safely, turn on hazard lights and call 911
explanation: Protect the scene and get help.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: Your right wheels drop off the pavement edge. You should:
choices: Jerk the wheel left right away
Ease off the gas, hold steady, and steer back gently when slowed
Speed up to climb back on
explanation: Sudden steering can cause a roll or a crossover.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: A vehicle is heading toward you in your lane. You should usually:
choices: Slow down and steer to the right
explanation: Moving right avoids crossing into other traffic.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: Your car goes into deep water. You should first:
choices: Wait for the car to fill with water
Call for help on your phone
Unbuckle and open the window to get out
explanation: Escape quickly before water pressure seals the doors.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: You hit an unattended parked car. You must:
choices: Drive away if the damage is minor
Leave your name and address and report it
Wait an hour for the owner
Leave only if no one saw
explanation: Drivers must identify themselves after damaging property.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC)

question: You must report a crash to police when:
choices: Only if there was a fire
Only if it was your fault
explanation: Crashes with injury or death must be reported.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.249

question: Your vehicle breaks down on a highway. You should:
choices: Stay in your lane with lights off
Walk on the travelled lane to get help
Move off the road if you can and turn on hazard lights
Stand behind your car in the lane
explanation: Get out of traffic and make your vehicle visible.
source: Learn to Drive Smart ch.8 (emergency strategies)

question: A fire truck has stopped at a fire. You must not drive within:
choices: 150 m of it on the same road
explanation: Keep clear of firefighting operations.
source: Motor Vehicle Act (BC) s.198

question: Before changing lanes, you should:
explanation: Mirrors, signal and a shoulder check are all required before a lane change.
source: Combines bank questions 171

question: You must NOT park within:
choices: 6 m of the approach side of a crosswalk
15 m of the nearest rail of a railway crossing
explanation: All three distances are parking limits in BC.
source: Combines bank questions 137, 138, 140

question: A Class 7L driver must:
choices: Display an L sign on the back of the vehicle
Have a qualified supervisor in the front passenger seat
Not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
explanation: All three are L restrictions.
source: Combines bank questions 114, 116, 117

question: Which of these affect how quickly your blood alcohol rises?
explanation: Body weight and food affect absorption; the drink's colour does not.
source: Combines bank questions 111

question: Ice often forms first on:
explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces.
source: Combines bank questions 189

question: Turning left on a green light with no arrow, you must yield to:
choices: Pedestrians crossing the road you turn onto
explanation: A left turn on a plain green yields to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
source: Combines bank questions 54

question: "Slow down, move over" applies to stopped vehicles showing flashing:
choices: Red or blue lights, such as police or ambulances
Yellow lights, such as tow trucks
explanation: The rule covers red, blue, yellow or white flashing lights.
source: Combines bank questions 216

question: BC's minimum passing-distance rules protect:
explanation: The rules cover pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and scooter riders.
source: Combines bank questions 206

question: Before turning right, check your right side for:
choices: Nothing, if your signal is on
explanation: Cyclists and pedestrians on your right are easy to miss.
source: Combines bank questions 224

question: An L or N driver may NOT:
choices: Use a hands-free phone while driving
Drive with any alcohol in their system
explanation: GLP drivers have zero alcohol and drugs and no electronic devices.
source: Combines bank questions 94, 96, 118, 124

question: You must have your headlights on:
choices: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
Whenever you cannot see clearly for 150 m
Only when it is fully dark
explanation: Both the time rule and the 150 m visibility rule apply.
source: Combines bank questions 182, 183

question: Which of these help prevent hydroplaning?
explanation: Lower speed and good tires help; cruise control in rain does not.
source: Combines bank questions 187

question: A school bus ahead has flashing red lights. You must stop if you are:
choices: Meeting it from the other direction
explanation: Traffic behind and meeting the bus must stop.
source: Combines bank questions 207

question: Before opening your door after parking on a street, check for:
explanation: An opened door can strike a cyclist or vehicle passing.
source: Combines bank questions 149

question: Which of these can slow your reaction time while driving?
explanation: Alcohol, drugs and tiredness all slow reactions.
source: Combines bank questions 105, 106, 194

question: Which are legal places to park?
choices: At a curb 7 m from a crosswalk
explanation: 3 m from a hydrant is too close; the other two are legal.
source: Combines bank questions 146, 151

question: When following a large truck, you should:
choices: Stay where you can see its mirrors
Keep at least 3 seconds behind it
Pass on its right when it swings left
explanation: Stay visible and well back; never pass a turning truck on the right.
source: Combines bank questions 181, 209, 210
